title: Concentrated vs Distributed Failures: Does One Monitor Threshold Fit Both?

original_idea.body:
# Concentrated vs Distributed Failures: Does One Monitor Threshold Fit Both?

**Problem:** UK AISI distinguishes concentrated safety failures (one catastrophic action) from distributed failures (many small harmful actions), arguing they need different monitoring. No one has empirically shown a single monitor threshold trades off badly between the two.

**Direction:** Construct two synthetic agentic task sets: one with rare high-severity sabotage and one with frequent low-severity harmful nudges. Run a single suspicion-scoring monitor and show the safety/usefulness frontier for each, demonstrating whether a threshold tuned for concentrated failures misses distributed ones (and vice versa). Propose a simple dual-threshold rule.

**Why it matters:** Empirically grounding the concentrated/distributed distinction guides monitoring design directly. Synthetic tasks + inference keep it feasible and lab-independent, addressing a named open problem.

**Relevant context:** Context file Open Problems: 'Detect concentrated safety failures vs. distributed failures — different monitoring approaches needed (UK AISI AI Control research areas)'.
